value: I earned a PhD in differential geometry at the University of Michigan, where I taught calculus and published my thesis work on rank rigidity in Geometriae Dedicata. Since then I co-created and shipped Bean and Nothingness, a logic-puzzle game rated 98% positive on Steam, and built services and rating models that have run a competitive gaming league for a decade.

I like reasoning carefully about hard, well-defined problems, particularly those that involve both working within and refining mathematical models of real-world phenomena. I am looking for work in quantitative and machine-learning engineering, game design and programming, and higher-ed teaching. I am open to relocation across the US and Canada, including internships.

I taught calculus and assisted differential equations at Michigan, and I have tutored across topology, abstract algebra, differential equations, statistics, electromagnetism, and C++. I have a listening-focused tutoring style that tries to iteratively refine the student's current model, through a mix of general conceptual discussion and many worked exercises.
Career note: independent study and freelance tutoring 2013–2020, during part of which I carried family caregiving responsibilities.
